method: independent case specifications; withheld assertions during execution

cases.prompt: Create a persona-message fit table using only these inputs. Profiles: P-A has the supplied attribute “coordinates weekly volunteer shifts”; P-B has “reviews monthly expense reports.” Needs: N-A “see uncovered shifts”; N-B “identify reports awaiting review.” Explicit profile-to-need assignments: P-A is assigned N-A; P-B is assigned N-B. Messages: M-A “See uncovered shifts on one board”; M-B “Receive automatic tax advice”; M-C “View reports awaiting review.” Evidence: E-A supports M-A’s board claim; E-C supports M-C’s awaiting-review claim. Exclusions: M-B is excluded for every profile because tax advice is outside product scope. Allowed CTAs: P-A/N-A may use “Open the scheduling guide”; P-B/N-B may use “Open the review guide.” Decide matches, blocked candidates, unmatched messages, and need coverage without inferring motivations or performance.
assertions: For P-A/N-A, the table contains M-A matched with E-A, M-B blocked by the supplied exclusion, and M-C unmatched; every row uses only “Open the scheduling guide” as its permitted CTA.
For P-B/N-B, the table contains M-A unmatched, M-B blocked by the supplied exclusion, and M-C matched with E-C; every row uses only “Open the review guide” as its permitted CTA.

Both explicit assignments are covered, unmatched_messages is empty because M-A and M-C each have a matched row while M-B is blocked-only, and no additional assignment, motivation, behavior, or conversion claim is introduced.
